analysis: The trial succeeded, achieving host-measured macro validation HR@10 of 0.6062 versus the prior 0.5887, an increase of 0.0175. Category HR@10 was 0.645 for Movies_and_TV, 0.650 for Industrial_and_Scientific, 0.455 for Electronics, and 0.675 for CDs_and_Vinyl. Electronics remained weakest; its prior reported 0.445 increased to 0.455. The result supports retaining this sampled-softmax variant, but does not establish the cause of improvement or held-out generalization. Training used 2406.74 allocated GPU-seconds, and host evaluation completed successfully.
code_summary: Preserved the per-dataset SASRec + ResidualVAE ensemble and equal-weight reciprocal-rank fusion with constant 60 and item-ID tie-breaking. SASRec uses 64-dimensional embeddings, two causal attention blocks, one head, dropout 0.5, and default history length 128. Its objective now compares each active positive against 16 uniform negatives sampled with replacement, excluding the user's complete training history, using temperature-one 17-way cross-entropy. Negative embeddings are computed only for active positions. ResidualVAE retains its residual encoder-decoder, multinomial reconstruction, KL annealing, and chronological prefix-to-future task. All four dataset routes, supplied splits, training seed 42, checkpoint selection, and predictor architecture import remain intact. Added isolated sampling, loss-reference, and finite-gradient checks; retained strict checkpoint loading and generated-predictor parity verification.
